reason: The hypothesis makes specific claims about native oxide film behavior on Q235 steel, but the cited evidence (E1, E2) only concerns HEA coatings on Q235 substrates, not the native oxide or its temperature-dependent breakdown. E3 is about HEA coating cracking and erosion, offering no support. Thus, none of the key premises are supported by the cited passages.
premises: Native Fe-oxide film quality (continuity, adhesion) governs corrosion onset in Q235 steel
Microstructural features (grain boundaries, inclusions) modulate native oxide film properties
At room temperature, a continuous adherent oxide suppresses corrosion (lower current, minimal pitting)
At elevated temperature, thermal stress induces film breakdown, increasing corrosion and pitting
Mild pre-oxidation reinforces the oxide barrier, improving corrosion resistance over untreated native oxide
